Nephrotic syndrome: 4

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A nephrotic patient has substantially elevated cholesterol despite no recent dietary change. Which metabolic feature commonly accompanies heavy proteinuria and hypoalbuminemia as part of the systemic consequences of the syndrome?

  1. Nephrotic syndrome
  2. Reduced plasma oncotic pressure
  3. Hypercoagulability
  4. Increased infection susceptibility
  5. Increased circulating lipids
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Increased circulating lipids

Nephrotic syndrome can alter lipoprotein synthesis and clearance, producing hyperlipidemia.

Understanding the options

Increased circulating lipids
Nephrotic syndrome can alter lipoprotein synthesis and clearance, producing hyperlipidemia.
Nephrotic syndrome
Heavy proteinuria with hypoalbuminemia and edema defines the core nephrotic pattern, often with hyperlipidemia. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Reduced plasma oncotic pressure
Urinary albumin loss contributes to edema; renal sodium retention also matters. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Hypercoagulability
Urinary loss of anticoagulant proteins and other changes increase venous thrombosis risk. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Increased infection susceptibility
Loss of immune proteins and some treatments increase infection risk in nephrotic patients. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
